open_points.subject: R0-90 disclosure classification
open_points.text: the alias is held as `business_confidential`, not `personal_data` ... Registry's guarantees that no `personal_data` value reaches an agent and that no other service keeps one cover the values it holds in that class
open_points.question: When an alias actually contains a customer's name, address or other identifying value, does its field classification remain `business_confidential`, or do the value-based `personal_data` guarantees in R0-25, R0-26 and R0-80 forbid sending it to the agent and keeping it in another service?
options: Classification follows the alias field, so the value reaches the agent and may remain in a consumer snapshot
Classification follows the actual content, so the value is `personal_data` and must not reach the agent or be kept by another service
The alias remains `business_confidential`, but a detected breach triggers separate containment rules
open_points.default_guess: Treat the alias field as `business_confidential` regardless of content, because R0-90 explicitly says Registry does not inspect it and permits both disclosures.

witness.initial: A customer is named Ana García, and the project has no alias.
events: The owner sets the alias to "Ana García", which is at most 40 characters.
Registry accepts it because it checks only length.
The agent reads the project projection and a consumer stores its permitted snapshot.
outcomes: R0-90 permits the agent to receive the alias and the consumer to keep it because the alias field is `business_confidential`.
The value-based promises that no `personal_data` value reaches an agent and no other service keeps the customer's name forbid those results.
witness.observer: The customer, agent and snapshot-holding consumer see the difference.

open_points.subject: R0-90 violating-alias remediation
open_points.text: the owner's rule on its content is the rest, and Registry promises nothing further about a value that breaks it
open_points.question: What Registry action can the owner use to replace or clear an accepted alias after discovering that it contains a person's name, an address or another identifying value?
options: The ordinary project-correction action can set, replace and clear the alias
An accepted alias cannot be changed
Registry deliberately provides no remediation action
open_points.default_guess: Allow the owner to replace or clear the alias through project correction, with the project's normal revision and audit rules.

witness.initial: A project has an accepted alias containing a customer's name.
events: The owner discovers the breach and attempts to remove the identifying value.
outcomes: An implementation treats alias as a correctable project field and lets the owner replace or clear it.
An implementation reads "promises nothing further" literally and provides no alias-remediation action.
witness.observer: The owner and the affected customer see whether the identifying alias can be removed from future Registry answers.

open_points.subject: R0-90 downstream copies after alias correction
open_points.text: an alias whose content breaks the rule does reach the agent and a consumer's kept snapshot ... Registry promises nothing further about a value that breaks it
open_points.question: After a violating alias is corrected or cleared in Registry, what must happen to the old value already held in a consumer snapshot or exposed to an agent session?
options: Consumers must delete or refresh the value immediately
A consumer replaces it on its next project read
The old snapshot may remain until the consumer's ordinary retention ends
No downstream correction or deletion obligation exists
open_points.default_guess: Require consumers to replace the alias on their next project read, while acknowledging that Registry cannot retract an earlier agent disclosure.

witness.initial: A consumer snapshot contains an alias that names the customer.
events: The owner corrects the alias in Registry.
The consumer remains offline and continues serving or using its existing snapshot.
outcomes: The consumer may retain and use the old alias indefinitely because R0-90 promises nothing further.
The consumer must purge or replace the old alias after correction because it contains a value the writer rule forbids.
witness.observer: The customer and users of the consumer see whether the old identifying alias remains visible.
